title: Glycan Masking and Colonization Assay
author: John Parkinson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j8ucrww
materials: Using ImageJ software, run the thee provided macros to a. mask out the polyp mouth area, b. count the number of symbiont cells, and c. calculate the host tissue area. Divide cell counts by their respective host tissue areas to calculate symbiont cell density for each polyp.

steps.title: Prepare aposymbiotic anemones
steps.instruction: Place aposymbiotic anemones (~0.5 mm oral disc diameter) one per well in a 24‑well plate containing 1 mL filtered seawater (FSW); seal with Parafilm, keep in darkness at room temperature overnight to allow attachment.

steps.title: Prepare Symbiodinium cultures
steps.instruction: Either the day of the experiment or 1 day prior, harvest Symbiodinium from cultures at 1e6 cells·mL‑1; allocate 1 mL media per polyp in the treatment and place subcultures in 15 mL Falcon tubes (split into multiple tubes if needed).

steps.title: Mask glycans with lectins
steps.instruction: Approximately 2 h before the experiment, centrifuge the subcultures at 1500 RCF for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in lectin solution (100 µg·mL‑1; 0.33 mL lectin per 1e6 cells). Incubate for 2 h, vortexing gently every 20 min. After incubation, centrifuge again as before, resuspend in FSW to 1e6 cells·mL‑1, and repeat the wash at least once more.

substeps.instruction: Remove supernatant and add lectin (100 µg·mL‑1, 0.33 mL per 1e6 cells).
Incubate 2 h with gentle vortex every 20 min.
Centrifuge again, resuspend in FSW to 1e6 cells·mL‑1.
Repeat the wash at least once.

steps.title: Add treated symbionts to anemones
steps.instruction: Remove the FSW from each anemone well and add 1 mL of the lectin‑treated Symbiodinium suspension (1e6 cells·mL‑1). Add 10 µL of Artemia directly above each polyp, reseal with Parafilm, and incubate at 26 °C under a 12:12 L:D photoperiod with 15 µmol quanta·m‑2·s‑1.

steps.title: Dilute and re‑oxygenate after 24 h
steps.instruction: After 24 h (1 day post‑exposure), add an additional 1 mL of FSW to each well, reseal the plate, and return it to the incubator.

steps.title: Transfer to fresh FSW on day 2
steps.instruction: After another 24 h (2 days post‑exposure), move each anemone to a new 24‑well plate containing fresh 1 mL FSW per well; while transferring, gently remove any Symbiodinium adhering to the polyp surface, especially the sticky ring, using fine forceps. Seal and return to the incubator.

steps.title: Relax and fix polyps on day 3
steps.instruction: After a further 24 h (3 days post‑exposure), replace the FSW with 1 mL relaxing solution (0.376 M MgCl₂ in FSW) and allow polyps to relax for 10 min. Transfer each polyp to ~30 µL of 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS (in a 0.5 mL tube) at room temperature, ensuring the volume covers the entire polyp. Incubate 1 h, then replace fixative with PBS and store polyps at 20 °C overnight.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL 0.376 M MgCl₂ in FSW; relax 10 min.
Transfer polyp to ~30 µL 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS (0.5 mL tube).
Incubate 1 h, replace with PBS, store at 20 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare samples for microscopy
steps.instruction: Using small dissection scissors, separate the polyp body from the “head” (oral disc and tentacles). Mount the head on a slide with glycerol mountant (90 % glycerol in PBS), spreading the oral disc and tentacles flat with minimal overlap.

steps.title: Capture fluorescence images
steps.instruction: With an epifluorescent microscope at 5× objective, acquire separate .jpg images of the red channel (symbiont chlorophyll fluorescence) and the green channel (host GFP fluorescence).
